title: Career summary from lessons to the Oliver band and Shanghai
summary: Nicholas recounts lessons with Wooden Joe and the Tios, early bands, the Navy, his own group, King Oliver in Chicago, Shanghai and the trip home.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, I started taking lessons around 9 years of age with my uncle, Wooden Joe Nicholas. He was my big influence on this jazz scene. And later on, I went to Papa Teo and took lessons with him for about a couple of years. Then Lorenzo Teo, his son. And finished up with him until around 1915. Then I started to go pro. My first gigs around New Orleans was with the Maple Leaf Band. Then Buddy Petite's Band. When Jimmy Noon left to go to Chicago, I played with Buddy Petite and several other bands around New Orleans. In fact, nearly all of them until 1917. And I went to Navy for three years during World War I. Studied a little bit. Played in the Navy Band. And came out in 1919. In December. Played with Buddy Petite again. And then formed a little group of my own. With Barney B. Godd on tenor we were learning in Saxton. And Louie Russell, Paul Barberin, Willie Santiago, Alnorma Twai on trumpet. And spent a year or so at Anderson until King Oliver sent for us to come to Chicago. And stayed with them, with King Oliver until 1926, August. And went to Shanghai, China with Jack Carter. The latest note, Terry Weatherford, Billy Page, Frank Etheridge. And had a wonderful year at the Plaza Hotel in Shanghai. Afterwards, instead of coming back to America by the way of California. We got our transportation. Mine was until Marseille, France. I was on my own afterwards. But anyhow, I was stopped in Egypt and India and Singapore, Sumatra, Malay. And finally arrived in Marseille in October 1928. Went to Paris and stayed a week waiting for my boat from Schilberg to go to New York. Had a wonderful surprise, seeing Sidney, my old sidekick.
